acceptanceCriteria: The cause is determined from the observer teardown order (zombie before reap versus a real survivor) and recorded in the ticket or a build-log entry
TestAFUV0NoDescendantsOnInterruption distinguishes a reap-pending descendant from a surviving one, with a bounded wait, and passes 20 consecutive -race runs on hosted ubuntu
If a real leak is found, the observer kills its descendants before returning from an interrupted observation and a regression test covers it
body: Suspected flake, not a confirmed defect. Hosted CI run 38494366263 (PR beamfall/corvint#870, go-product-shard (6), ubuntu-24.04, go test -race -p 1 under test-confine) failed internal/appflows TestAFUV0NoDescendantsOnInterruption: `observer_unix_test.go:83: descendant 64508 survived interruption` and `descendant 64515 survived interruption` (0.64s). The AFP-V0-047 outcomes rerun of the whole package passed at once (ci-outcomes-pull_request-6: rerun.state RAN, internal/appflows pass), and the PR touches no internal/appflows path. Expected: after cancel() returns through done, no observer descendant answers syscall.Kill(pid, 0). Actual: both descendants still answered. Inference (unverified): kill(pid, 0) succeeds for a zombie until it is reaped, and the test checks immediately after the observation returns, so a descendant still in teardown or awaiting reap reads as survived; a bounded poll (for example up to 2s until Kill returns ESRCH) or reaping before the check would separate a real leak from the race. Reproduction: rerun the package under -race on a loaded ubuntu runner; local darwin runs did not reproduce in this session. Version: origin/main 5163d1ed4 plus PR #870 head c6fe57654.
title: Suspected flake: TestAFUV0NoDescendantsOnInterruption reports descendants that survived interruption on hosted ubuntu (PR #870 shard 6)
